D020-D013_h001.question:
It’s been… I’d say a couple of months now that I just haven’t felt like myself. Ever since everything started changing with my living situation and my health, I feel on edge most of the time. I wake up already tense, like my shoulders are up by my ears, and my mind starts racing before I’m even out of bed—worrying about money, my blood pressure, being alone in the house, you name it.

I’ve always been a bit of a worrier, even back when I was on the ward, but this feels different. There’s this constant nervousness, like I’ve had too much coffee, even when I haven’t. I catch myself fiddling with my hands or pacing the hallway without realizing it. When my daughter leaves after visiting, I get this panicky, knotted feeling in my stomach; I hate seeing her go, and I start imagining something happening to me and no one noticing.

I wouldn’t say I’m completely unable to enjoy things—I still watch my shows and talk to my neighbor—but there’s a heaviness there, and I get tired more easily. Some days I just sit and stare at the garden, thinking too much, feeling low and jumpy at the same time.

A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D020-D013_h001.answer: B & C. Adjustment Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

I worry a lot about the future, but I also feel weirdly numb, like I’m watching my life from the outside and can’t quite care enough to change anything.

D020-D013_h024.question:
It’s been… I’d say a couple of months now that I’ve just not felt like myself. It started sometime after the new school year began—there were a lot of changes, staff turnover, new curriculum—and since then I’ve been on edge and down at the same time.

Most days I wake up with this tight feeling in my chest, already worrying about the day before I even get out of bed. Small things at work—an email from the district, a parent complaint—can send me into this spiral where my mind races and I feel almost shaky inside. But then, at other times, it’s like someone turned the volume down on everything. I go through the motions, but I feel kind of flat, like I’m underwater watching my own life.

I’m tired a lot, even though my sleep is hit or miss—some nights I’m lying there going over schedules and budgets, other nights I just crash early. I still go to work and get things done, but it takes more effort than it used to, and I don’t really enjoy the parts I used to love, like being in the classrooms. At home my husband says I seem “distant.” I wouldn’t say I’m falling apart, but something’s not right and it’s not really lifting.

I’ve been driving way too fast, cutting people off, blowing through yellow lights like I don’t care what happens. Part of me almost doesn’t.

I’ve started doing things that are just… out of character.
